analysis.message: This 53-year-old T2 patient demonstrates a highly predictable pattern of post-lunch hypoglycemia occurring daily. The consistent timing and normal pre-lunch glucose strongly suggest iatrogenic hypoglycemia from sulfonylurea or glinide medication. Given obesity (111kg), switching to a GLP-1 RA would simultaneously eliminate the hypoglycemia risk, improve postprandial control, and promote significant weight loss.

patterns.name: Post-Lunch Hypoglycemia
patterns.evidence: Consistent hypoglycemic events (60-80 mg/dL) occurring daily at 15:00-15:45 on all 10 days, approximately 2-3 hours after lunch. Pre-lunch glucose is normal (102-125 mg/dL). Rescue carbohydrates required every day. Lunch intake is modest and consistent (salad, soup, wrap, quinoa bowl). Pattern is highly reproducible and predictable.
